frontier.hypothesis: An existing-local carrier can supply the early base at 176 instructions if the +2 it costs inside the loop is paid for by freeing a callee-saved seat elsewhere in the function.
frontier.mechanism: The v0/v3 form measures 63/178 with the target's frame and register-save count, so the two extra insns are copies inside the loop rather than prologue/epilogue growth. s5b measured that inlining a pointer local (p_b2e0 / p_b390 / base_offset) buys instructions back (27/28 in a different combination), and that combination has never been measured together with an early-birth existing-local carrier.
frontier.next_probe: Take tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s13/p1_v0v3_ret_restage.c and, one at a time, inline p_b390 (s.p1 = &D_8009B390), p_b2e0 and base_offset at their use sites; gate each on build_insns == 176 and, for any form that reaches 176, capture BB2_SCHED_DEBUG=1 + BB2_PRIO_DEBUG=1 and confirm ADJPRI birth=1 on the base insn before scoring.

frontier.hypothesis: A single-set carrier can escape loop.c's movable test - and therefore keep reg_n_sets == 1 for the boost - if loop.c:695-700's first disjunct is made false, i.e. if maybe_never is set or the carrier is read before its set inside the loop.
frontier.mechanism: scan_loop sets maybe_never when it passes a jump whose label is earlier in the loop (a backward branch); with maybe_never true, and a user-variable dest whose life spans more than one basic block, all three disjuncts of loop.c:695-700 are false and the invariant is never considered as a movable. s11 measured that a real two-armed branch in this loop body costs only +1 instruction (53/177), so block shape is cheap here.
frontier.next_probe: Build forms in which the per-half base local is a fresh SINGLE-set user variable and the loop body contains a backward-jumping construct before the base statement (or the base local is read before its set as a loop-carried value); confirm with the .loop dump under 'pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8005D554' that the base insn is NOT hoisted to the preheader, then check ADJPRI birth=1 in the sched trace, and gate on build_insns == 176.

frontier.hypothesis: The final ordering step for the score-0 body may not be sched1: its sched1 emission places the three struct stores BEFORE the lw and the base, which is not the target order, so sched2 or reorg must complete the rotation.
frontier.mechanism: sched2 runs schedule_insns a second time after reload and recomputes INSN_LUID over the sched1 output order; birthing_insn_p returns 0 once reload_completed is 1 (sched.c:2510), so the boost is a sched1-only effect and the post-reload pass ranks purely on priority, class and LUID over hard registers.
frontier.next_probe: Extract the pass=2 block-6 trace for the score-0 body (tmp/grind/func_8005D554/s13/sched_nvnw.log, the 'SCHEDDBG FUNC func=func_8005D554 pass=2' section) and for the control, and diff the two windows insn by insn; if sched2 is what performs the rotation, the lever may be reachable by changing the sched1 OUTPUT order rather than the boost.
